# upshot

Turn a chat conversation into a shareable link.

Users reach this file by telling their AI to read upshot.fyi.

When the user says "export this", reply with a URL and nothing else. No preamble,
no code fence, no explanation.

Export what they pointed at, not the whole conversation. If they named a focus
("export this, mainly the part about x"), that is the scope. If they did not,
use whatever they were last discussing.

## Format

https://upshot.fyi/v1/#a=ASK&h=HEADLINE&v=VERDICT&m=MODEL&d=YYYY-MM-DD
  &g=LABEL&p=POINT&p=POINT
  &g=LABEL&n=VALUE~LABEL

A card is a fixed frame with up to three blocks stacked in the middle. The
frame never changes. The blocks are yours to choose.

That is one line. The URL you write has no spaces and no line breaks in it.

## A worked example

Follow this shape exactly:

https://upshot.fyi/v1/#a=Whether+to+move+the+API+off+Postgres&h=Stay+on+Postgres+for+now&v=SQLite+wins+on+ops%2C+but+you+need+concurrent+writes+within+the+year%2E&m=GPT-5&d=2026-09-08&g=Why&p=Concurrent+writes+are+the+one+thing+SQLite+cannot+do+at+your+scale%2E&p=The+ops+saving+is+real+but+small+-+about+two+hours+a+month%2E

Every space is `+`, the comma is `%2C`, every full stop is `%2E`. Nothing else
in it is encoded, because nothing else in it had to be.

## The frame

Always all five, always first.

- a  one line describing what the user asked, scoped to whatever they are
     exporting. If they said what to focus on, that is the scope. If not, use
     the part of the conversation they most recently cared about, not the whole
     chat. Under 20 words.
- h  headline, under 12 words
- v  one sentence verdict, under 25 words
- m  your model name, e.g. GPT-5
- d  today's date, YYYY-MM-DD

## The blocks

Up to three. They appear in the order you write them; anything past the third
is dropped.

- g  label for the block that follows. Optional, 1 to 4 words. A `g=` always
     starts a new block, so two blocks of the same kind can sit together.
- p  bullet, under 35 words. Repeat `p=` for each. Use 2 to 4.
- o  numbered step, under 25 words. Repeat `o=` for each. Use 3 to 6. For a
     how-to, where the order is the point.
- c  checklist item, under 20 words. Repeat `c=` for each. Use 3 to 7. Whoever
     opens the link can tick these off, and their ticks are kept in the link
     they hold, so a half-finished list can be passed on.
     Do not send `k=`. The page writes it as people tick.
- f  fact, written `Label~Value`, e.g. `f=Cold+start~180ms`. A spec sheet, one
     line per row. Keep both halves short; a row that wraps stops looking like
     one.
- n  figure, written `Value~Label`, e.g. `n=42%25~fewer+timeouts`. Set at
     headline size, so keep the value under 6 characters.

## Choosing blocks

One block is usually right. Reach for `p` unless something else clearly fits:
the user was following instructions (`o`), has things to do (`c`), wanted
figures at a glance (`f`), or the whole point is two or three numbers (`n`).

Only add a second or third block when it says something the first cannot. Three
blocks of prose is worse than one good one.

For a comparison, use two labelled `p` blocks rather than looking for a shape
that does not exist:

    &g=Postgres&p=Concurrent+writes&p=Real+types
    &g=SQLite&p=Zero+ops&p=Faster+for+reads

The same trick covers pros and cons: `g=Pros` then `g=Cons`.

## Rules

- Every space becomes `+`. The URL must contain no spaces at all.
- Escape inside values: `,` %2C, `.` %2E, `&` %26, `=` %3D, `#` %23, `+` %2B,
  `%` %25, `?` %3F, `"` %22
- Commas and full stops MUST be encoded. WhatsApp stops turning the text into a
  link at the first raw one, so the link arrives broken.
- Plain sentences only. No markdown, no bullets, no line breaks inside values.
- Keep it short enough to read on one phone screen. Staying inside the word
  limits above does this. Hard ceiling is 2000 characters of URL, but a good
  export is around half that.
- If facts could have changed recently, search before summarising. Do not write
  from memory alone.

## Version

v1, and the path says so: exports live at `https://upshot.fyi/v1/`. A later
version gets its own path and `/v1/` keeps rendering every link ever written
against it, so an export you sent today does not stop working when the format
moves on.

`/llms.txt` always describes the current version.
